# Kapusta et al. (2025) — A Framework for the Assurance of AI-Enabled Systems (DoD CDAO)

> **External, not NASA governance.** Useful for comparison and vocabulary. It never establishes
> what NASA requires, and must not be cited as NASA coverage.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Publisher / owner** | Authors from the Office of the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer (CDAO), U.S. Department of Defense; The MITRE Corporation; Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory |
| **Kind** | Research / conference paper proposing a framework (not itself a DoD-issued policy document) |
| **Status** | Cleared for open publication 2025-03-11 by the DoD Office of Prepublication and Security Review (Case 25-T-1410); posted as arXiv:2504.16937v1, 2025-04-03. |
| **Where to get it** | Public: arXiv (2504.16937) and MITRE Public Release (Case 25-0757). Public copy, confirmed anonymously off-network on 2026-10-26: `https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.16937` |
| **Binds whom** | No one — a proposed framework, not an issued directive. |

**What it is good for, relative to NASA's documents.** The closest document among those mapped here to an assurance-case
vocabulary built specifically for AI systems, with its own glossary of terms (Assurance, Assurance
Case, Assurance Claim, Assured, Hazard, Mishap, Lifecycle) — several explicitly sourced to NIST AI RMF
and MIL-STD-882E (our reading).

**Key content for AI / machine-learning assurance.**
- Proposes a "claims-based framework for risk management and assurance of AI systems," built around a
  **top-level assurance claim**: "While operating within its defined scope, the system will achieve its
  intended outcomes without introducing unacceptable risks, throughout its lifecycle" (§2, Definition
  D-5 note, p.3, verbatim).
- Three phases of the AI assurance process, per its own Figure 1: **prepare for assurance, establish
  assurance, maintain assurance** (§1, p.2).
- Key definitions (§2, pp.2–4), each with a source where borrowed: AI System (sourced to NIST AI RMF),
  Hazard and Lifecycle (sourced to MIL-STD-882E, "modified"), Assurance, Assurance Case, Assurance
  Claim, Assurance Plan, Assured.
- States the framework is intended to balance "competing needs for faster deployment, successful
  adoption, and rigorous evaluation" (Abstract, p.1, verbatim in part) via "clear steps, a modular and
  iterative approach, tangible completion criteria, and explicit approval gates" (§1, p.2).
- Keywords list (p.1) names DODD 3000.09 (autonomous weapons policy), System-of-Systems, and Adversarial
  ML as topics the framework is meant to cover, without developing them in the excerpt reviewed here.

**Nearest NASA counterpart.** No NASA document has an equivalent AI-specific assurance-claim glossary;
compares most directly to
`../documents/NASA-STD-7009B.md`'s model-credibility framing (our reading, comparison only).
